daily_summary.html:
Domestic Politics

Coordinating Minister for Political, Legal and Security Affairs Mahfud MD proposed that contracts with food caterers (SPPG) be terminated and the free school meals (MBG) program management shifted to village governments, following a wave of food poisoning incidents. Separately, Mahfud also assessed that online gambling crimes should be included in the draft Asset Forfeiture Bill. The Deputy Minister for Human Rights stated that student safety and security must be a priority in implementing the free meals program.

  • The MPR urged real action on disability discount policy implementation.
  • An analyst at Kompas examined Gerindra party's institutionalization challenges in relation to West Java Governor Dedi Mulyadi.
  • The KPK examined the Bengkulu City DPRD chairman about his core duties in an ongoing investigation.
  • A DPR member stated that village head terms should remain limited to give opportunities to new generations, rejecting proposals for unlimited terms.
  • New allegations emerged in the Unsoed case, with claims that a regional secretary knew about extortion and a high school teacher acted as a collector.
  • Minister of Primary and Secondary Education announced that part-time PPPK teachers will become full-time in 2027, with budget already allocated.
  • Social Affairs Minister Maruarar said the target for house renovation programs jumped from 45,000 to 400,000 units this year.

Foreign Policy & Defence

President Prabowo arrived in India to attend the 18th BRICS Summit. India's ambassador to Indonesia said the BRICS agenda aligns with Indonesia-India bilateral focus and called Indonesia a key Global South voice in BRICS. India also invited Indonesia to expand AI cooperation within BRICS.

  • An Indonesian lawmaker welcomed Malaysia's offer to help fight wildfires in Indonesia.
  • The Army Chief of Staff denied that three civil servants killed in Papua were military intelligence, calling such claims an excuse by armed groups.
  • Police designated two individuals as wanted suspects in the shooting of civil servants in Papua.
  • DPR members urged full investigation into the armed group shooting of three civil servants in Jayawijaya.
  • The Saudi Ambassador prayed for the safety of five missing Indonesian journalists near Mount Anak Krakatau.

Other

A massive food poisoning outbreak linked to the free school meals program continued to spread, with 352 elementary students in Central Lombok suspected of poisoning and the caterer facing suspension. Police examined the caterer in Pati following hundreds of suspected poisoning cases, while meals in Sidoarjo tested positive for bacterial contamination. The government is working to find ideal kitchen scales for the national free meal program to improve food safety standards.

  • Indonesia's lobster farming trial opens a path to exports to Singapore.
  • The Tourism Minister sought more investment in priority destinations and special economic zones.
  • Immigration and police detained 31 foreign nationals over online fraud operations.
  • The Ministry of Environment boosted air quality monitoring following the Mount Anak Krakatau eruption.
  • A manufacturing industry credit grew 16.85 percent, becoming a pillar for the banking sector.
